survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This OECD TALIS Starting Strong 2024 participant note reports descriptive survey results from questionnaires administered to early childhood education and care (ECEC) staff and setting leaders in participating pre-primary settings (ISCED 02) and, in some entities, settings for children under age 3. The note states that the survey aims to obtain a representative sample in each participating country and subnational entity, but it does not report the specific sampling weight variable names or any replicate-weight scheme (e.g., BRR/jackknife). Because the document is a descriptive results note rather than a student-level predictive model, it does not specify how analysts should apply weights in estimation; however, for OECD/TALIS Starting Strong database users, the appropriate approach is to use the survey weights provided with the TALIS Starting Strong 2024 database to account for the complex sampling design and non-response. The note also flags that estimates should be interpreted with caution due to higher risk of non-response bias, which is consistent with the need for proper weighted estimation.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible values are not applicable because this participant note reports questionnaire-based descriptive indicators (e.g., percentages of staff/leaders reporting stress, training needs, satisfaction, and communication practices) rather than cognitive achievement scores that are typically scaled using PVs. Missing-data handling is not reported because the note does not describe any imputation or deletion strategy; it focuses on indicator presentation and does not provide methodological details on missing responses.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The note focuses on Finland’s TALIS Starting Strong 2024 results for ECEC settings at the pre-primary level (centre-based early childhood education for ages 0–6 and pre-primary education for ages 6–7, ISCED 02). It does not provide the analytic sample size or explicit inclusion/exclusion rules (e.g., response completeness thresholds), so the filtering criteria are not fully specified in the provided text.

data.outcome_summary: TALIS Starting Strong 2024 is an OECD large-scale survey using questionnaires administered to ECEC staff and setting leaders to capture background, training, daily work, and self-reported practices and well-being in early childhood education and care. In Finland, the note covers centre-based ECEC for children aged 0–6 and pre-primary education for children aged 6–7 (ISCED 02), and it reports indicator-based comparisons with other participating countries and subnational entities. The results highlight that family engagement practices are frequent (e.g., events for families/visits at least several times a year in 84% of settings; informal communication monthly in ~90% of settings), and that staff report lower stress than in other entities (40% reporting stress “quite a bit” or “a lot”). Workforce retention concerns are linked to staffing shortages and absences (e.g., leaders citing staff absences as hindrances in 38% of settings; leaders citing lack of human resources as a stress source in 65%). The note also cautions that estimates may be affected by higher non-response bias, and it does not provide technical details on weighting, missing-data handling, or any predictive modeling.
data.null_fields_interpretation: This document is a country participant note summarizing descriptive survey indicators from TALIS Starting Strong 2024 rather than an empirical predictive/causal analysis. As a result, there is no student-level outcome modeling, no machine-learning pipeline, and no reported PV or missing-data handling strategy in the provided text. The absence of sample sizes and weight variable names reflects that the note is designed for interpretation of indicator results, while technical sampling and estimation details are typically provided in the full TALIS Starting Strong 2024 report/database documentation.
